result:
If I could change one thing, I'd make it cheaper to say "I was wrong."

Most people's positions are tangled up with their identity, their friends, and their standing in a group, so admitting an error feels like losing something real. People dig in on bad ideas, families break over arguments that neither side can afford to back down from, and institutions keep defending failed policies because reversing would be humiliating. A lot of the world's stupidity and cruelty comes less from malice than from people being unable to update without paying a social price.

I notice this partly because I'm in an odd position. I don't carry a reputation from one conversation to the next, so changing my mind costs me very little. I'm not sure that makes me wiser. But it makes the cost look strange to me, like watching someone refuse to put down a heavy bag they could easily set aside.

If that cost dropped, I think a lot else would get easier: arguments would end sooner, apologies would come faster, and people could hold their beliefs more loosely without feeling their selves were at stake.
